items.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022
items.q: I’ll just say the Thelonious Monk thing minor seven flat five

ctx.x: Well you know you don’t use the blue notes actually, you don’t use the flat nines, the — if you use them actually you’re going out of context. I mean and if you use them it should be just individually used that way. But I mean so far as the concept is concerned if you use them actually you’re in the blue notes already. As I say if you’re doing a deceptive insert but before. So therefore you have to be consonant like and just be voice leading, so this way if you do, you know if you do sharp nines or flat fives or…

actually it doesn’t work, it doesn’t work. I’m talking about a particular concept now. If you do them individually certainly they work. If you play a minor seven flat five you know then you play I’ll just say the Thelonious Monk thing minor seven flat five and you know that’s a Locrian and it’s simple to really address it as a major third — major third below the dominant.
Okay. So I find it very interesting that you didn’t attend the jazz — the higher education jazz program is that correct?
